newsitem.title: FINLAND: POLL - FINNISH 2006 BOND YIELD SEEN LOWER BY JUNE.
newsitem.headline: POLL - FINNISH 2006 BOND YIELD SEEN LOWER BY JUNE.

text.p: The Finnish 2006 benchmark bond yield is expected to trade lower, around 5.85 percent, three months from now compared to its current level at 5.97 percent, according to a Reuters poll.
By March next year, the yield was seen at around 6.25 percent and the trading range during the coming 12 months was mostly forecast to be 5.63-6.43 percent.
Half, 12 of 23 dealers, analysts and economists at banks and corporate treasury departments, expected the 2006 bond yield to trade at 5.90 percent or below by early June.
One saw it falling to 5.50 percent while eight market operators projected a rise to 6.00 percent or above.
The median of forecasts was 5.80 percent in a 5.50-6.40 percent range with the mean at 5.87 percent.
Looking one year ahead, the 2006-bond yield was expected to rise to 6.28 percent on average. The 23 forecasts ranged from 5.30 to 7.00 percent and the median was 6.25 percent.
Four expected the 2006 yield to fall to 5.50 percent or below while three forecast the yield to be as high as 7.00 percent at the start of March 1998.
Participants were also asked about the 12-month trading range for the 2006 bond yield. The median of lows was 5.63 percent while the median of highs was 6.43 percent.
The lows were in a 5.20-6.00 percent range and the highs in a 6.05-7.50 percent range.
Sixteen respondents put the low between 5.50 and 5.75 percent.
The poll was conducted by telephone on February 27. Forecasts were collected on an anonymous basis.

(London), Interbank, IVO, Kemira, Kesko, Merita Bank, Neste, Nokia, OKOBANK, Postipankki, SE-Banken (Helsinki), SOK, Unibank (Copenhagen) and UPM-Kymmene.
